qa.question:
According to the chairman's statement, as at the date of the annual report, the group had 
received booking fees for 63 residential units, of which 50 sale and purchase agreements 
(SPAs) had been completed, representing aggregate contracted sales of approximately $11.4 
million. A further nine residential units had been reserved, pending payment of the 
applicable booking fees. In addition, six commercial shophouses had been reserved for sale 
to the group's minority shareholders on an arm's-length basis. 
 
Note 19 of the financial statements reported revenue of $2.737 million from property 
development in Timor-Leste for FY2026. 
 
(Source: company annual report; emphasis added) 
 
The maiden recognition of revenue from the group's ongoing property development project 
in Timor-Leste was also identified as a key contributor to the improvement in the group's 
financial performance in FY2026. 
 
(i) 
Could management clarify how many residential units contributed to the 
$2.737 million of property development revenue recognised in FY2026? The 
63-unit sale figure mentioned in the chairman’s statement has a later cut-off at 
the date of the annual report. Is the booking fee 30% of the selling price?  
 
(ii) 
What were the achieved selling prices per square foot or square metre, and 
how did these compare with the selling prices assumed in the original 
feasibility study? 

(iii) 
Could management provide a breakdown of the buyer profile for the 63 
residential units, including the proportion of local and foreign buyers, 
individual purchasers and corporate entities?

Note 24 of the financial statements disclosed that, as at 31 July 2026, the group had $35.1 
million of contracted development expenditure that had not yet been provided for in the 
financial statements.  
 
 
(Source: company annual report) 
 
As at 31 July 2026, the group had cash and cash equivalents of $10.7 million. 
 
(i) 
How much has the group spent to date on the development of Timor Marina 
Square, and how much additional expenditure is required to complete the 
project? How does the remaining funding requirement compare with the 
group's available financial resources?  
 
During the year, it also obtained short-term working capital loans totalling approximately 
$13.4 million from Ma Jing, the daughter of the group's major shareholder, Mr Ma Weidong. 
The loans comprised $5.6 million carrying interest at 6% per annum and $7.84 million 
carrying interest at 3% per annum. 
 
(ii) 
How were the respective interest rates of 6% and 3% determined?   
 
On 18 June 2026, the company announced a proposed renounceable, non-underwritten 
rights issue of up to 268.3 million new ordinary shares at $0.10 per share, on the basis of one 
rights share for every existing share held. The proposed rights issue is expected to raise 
gross proceeds of approximately $26.53 million, before issue expenses. The net proceeds are 

intended to repay outstanding loans from a controlling shareholder and fund the group's 
ongoing property development in Timor-Leste. 
 
The previous rights issue in 2024 received valid acceptances for only 72.9% of the shares 
offered. 
 
(iii) 
What specific changes has the board made to address shareholders' 
concerns and improve participation in the proposed 1-for-1 rights issue? 
How will the company demonstrate that the proposed fundraising is 
supported by a credible business plan, realistic development milestones 
and an adequate expected return on shareholders' additional capital?

The company has announced that, as part of its board renewal process, Mr Loo Kenneth 
and Mr Sam Chong Keen will retire at the forthcoming AGM on 27 November 2026 and will 
not seek re-election. Mr Loo has served on the board for an aggregate period of nine years 
since his first appointment on 2 August 2017, while Mr Sam has served for more than 20 
years. 
 
In addition, Mr Darlington Tseng Te-Lin has informed the nominating committee and the 
board of his intention to step down as a non-executive and non-independent director at the 
2027 AGM, in support of the board's progressive renewal. 
 
Following the retirement of Mr Loo Kenneth and Mr Sam Chong Keen, only one independent 
director, Mr Lam Kwong Fai, will remain on the board. Consequently, the audit committee, 
nominating committee and remuneration committee will each fall below the minimum 
required membership of three directors. The company has indicated that it will endeavour 
to fill the vacancies within two months and, in any event, no later than three months. 
 
(i) 
What is the nominating committee's (NC's) board succession plan, and when 
did it commence the search for suitable candidates to fill the independent 
director positions? 

(Source: https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/quote/BQC.SI/) 
 
In 2016, there was a restructuring of the management team and an expansion of core 
businesses. 
 
(ii) 
What has been the total shareholder return over the past five and ten years 
(since the restructuring)?  
 
(iii) 
Has the NC undertaken a comprehensive review of the board's collective 
skills and competencies against the group's current strategic priorities and 
business risks? What material gaps, if any, have been identified? 
 
(iv) 
What specific criteria will the NC apply when selecting new independent 
directors, particularly in assessing their independence, relevant industry 
experience, financial and risk oversight capabilities, and ability to 
contribute effectively to the board and its committees?
